title: LLM Request v1
description: A closed provider-agnostic request configuration for one bounded language-model completion. Source-bearing values may be literal strings or repository-approved file references resolved by the runtime; credentials, when supplied, remain in memory and are never persisted, logged, prompted, or returned.

schema.description: The versioned identifier for this normalized LLM request contract.

provider.description: Provider adapter identity. The runtime defaults this field to openrouter when it is omitted.

model.description: Provider-specific model identifier. The runtime defaults this field to openai/gpt-5.6-luna when it is omitted.

thinking.description: Provider-independent reasoning effort. Adapters translate this value into provider-specific settings; the runtime defaults it to high.

maxFailedAttempts.description: Maximum number of provider invocations that fail before returning a provider or exhausted-attempts result. The runtime defaults this field to 3.

maxIterations.description: Maximum number of successful provider roundtrips, including correction requests after schema-invalid output. The runtime defaults this field to 3.

credentials.description: Optional in-memory provider credentials. The provider adapter may fall back to provider-specific environment variables when this field is omitted; implementations must not persist, log, prompt, or return these values.

task.description: Task data supplied to the model as a literal string or as a repository-approved file reference. When taskSchema is configured, the resolved content must be JSON and must validate against that schema before provider invocation.

systemPrompt.description: System-level instructions passed separately to the provider rather than embedded in the composed llmPrompt XML. This value may be literal content or a repository-approved file reference.
examples: You are an SDLC assessment agent. Return only JSON that conforms to outputSchema.

taskSchema.description: Optional task-data JSON Schema supplied as literal content or as a repository-approved file reference. When configured, the resolved task must parse as JSON and validate against it before provider invocation.

files.description: Ordered repository-approved reference files included in the composed llmPrompt. Declaration order is preserved, and each entry supplies the metadata used to label its CDATA body.

items.description: One ordered reference-file declaration included in the composed prompt.

examples.name: assessment-process
examples.purpose: Define assessment evidence and provider-fallback boundaries.

examples.name: assessment-process
examples.purpose: Define assessment evidence and provider-fallback boundaries.

outputSchema.description: Optional required-response JSON Schema supplied as literal content or as a repository-approved file reference. When configured, provider output must be JSON and must validate against the resolved schema before a successful response is returned.

Credentials.description: In-memory provider credential material accepted at the request boundary. The object intentionally permits only generic adapter inputs and must never be persisted, logged, placed in prompts, or returned.

apiKey.description: Provider API key held in memory for the duration of the request; it is redacted from diagnostics and excluded from all durable artifacts.

accessToken.description: Provider access token held in memory for the duration of the request; it is redacted from diagnostics and excluded from all durable artifacts.

ReferenceFile.description: Metadata for one ordered regular UTF-8 reference file resolved through the runtime's mediated read boundary.

name.description: Stable prompt-local label for the reference file.

path.description: Repository-relative regular-file path resolved by the mediated source boundary; absolute paths, traversal, and environment-file names are rejected by the runtime.

type.description: Lower-kebab-case semantic category used to label the reference body in the composed prompt.

purpose.description: Human-readable reason this file is supplied to the model.
examples: Define assessment evidence and provider-fallback boundaries.

examples.purpose: Define assessment evidence and provider-fallback boundaries.
